title: Word Squares
prompt:
Given an array of unique strings `words`, all of the same length, return all the word squares that can be formed using words from `words`. You may reuse a word from `words` as many times as needed when forming a square.

A sequence of strings forms a *word square* if the k-th row and k-th column read the same string, for every valid `k` from `0` to the square's size minus one. For example, `["ball","area","lead","lady"]` forms a word square because reading column 0 top-to-bottom gives "ball" (matches row 0), column 1 gives "area" (matches row 1), and so on.

Return the found squares as a list of lists of strings, in any consistent order produced by trying words in the given input order at each step (matching the standard backtracking traversal order).

examples.explanation: Both squares satisfy the row/column equality property; each uses 4 four-letter words from the list.
Both are valid 4x4 word squares built from the given words, with "baba" reused as both row 0 and row 2.

constraints: All words[i] have the same length
words[i] consists of only lowercase English letters
hints: Build the square row by row via backtracking. After placing rows 0..k-1, the required PREFIX of row k is fully determined: it must equal the string formed by taking character k from each of rows 0..k-1.

To quickly find all candidate words matching a required prefix (rather than scanning the whole word list at every step), insert all words into a trie and look up the prefix's node, then collect every word stored at or below it.

At each node of the trie, store the list of words that pass through it (built during insertion) so a prefix lookup is O(prefix length) plus the number of matches, instead of scanning all words linearly at every backtracking step.

solution.approach: Build a trie where each node stores the list of words passing through it (appended during insertion, so a node reached via some prefix P holds exactly the words starting with P). Backtrack row by row: having chosen rows 0..k-1, the next row must start with the prefix formed by taking the k-th character of each already-chosen row (this follows directly from the row/column equality requirement). Look up that prefix in the trie to get all valid candidate words in O(prefix length) time, then try each one recursively. A square is complete once n rows are chosen, where n is the word length. This prunes the search dramatically compared to trying every word at every row and checking validity afterward.
solution.timeComplexity: O(n * 26^n) worst case for building squares, bounded heavily in practice by trie pruning
solution.spaceComplexity: O(sum of word lengths) for the trie plus recursion depth
